title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: The assistant is mid-call, answering a student's question about the band saw. Which of these is actually part of its context window for this call?

options.text: The tool definitions it's currently allowed to call, since those were sent in with this request
A page of the manual it has not yet fetched with any tool call
A fact from a different student's conversation, happening in a separate session right now
Next month's maintenance schedule, since the assistant could need it eventually

items.stem: In one session, the assistant checks the dust collector's status, then a few turns later answers a question that depends on that same status. Why does it still have the right answer?

options.text: The model keeps a running memory of every tool result it has seen so far this session
The program re-fetches the dust collector's status automatically before every new turn
The status update, like the rest of the history, gets resent as text with every new call
The model's weights updated slightly once it saw the dust collector's status

items.stem: The assistant's context already holds the full transcripts of ten past bookings. A new student's question needs one fact from today's manual chapter. What's the best reason to leave the old transcripts out of this call?

options.text: Old transcripts are copyrighted, so the assistant isn't allowed to reuse them in a new call
Extra, irrelevant text makes the one needed fact harder to find and still costs tokens either way
The context window only accepts one topic of conversation at a time, by design
Transcripts expire after a fixed number of hours and stop being readable by the model

items.stem: A student's session ends Tuesday without the assistant writing anything to a file. On Thursday, they open a new session and ask a related question. In one sentence, what does the assistant's context window contain about Tuesday's conversation at the start of that new session?

Earlier, the assistant observed and wrote "the band saw blade was replaced on Oct 2" to a shop-status file. A student now asks if the blade is new, and the assistant reads that file back. What's the most accurate way to describe this read?

options.text: Only retrieval, since reading any file is always the same kind of tool call, regardless of content
Mechanically a retrieval-style tool call, but the content it returns is a note, since the agent itself wrote it
Only a note, since the agent wrote the fact, so no tool call is needed to read the file back
Neither, since writing the fact once already made it part of the model's trained knowledge
